newsitem.title: USA: U.S. phone stocks firm, helping 1996 performance.
newsitem.headline: U.S. phone stocks firm, helping 1996 performance.

text.p: Shares in regional Bells and long distance phone companies were stronger on Friday, helping a year-end catchup after their 1996 market underperformance. "The whole group is up across the board," said analyst Richard Klugman of brokers PaineWebber.
Regional Bells rose two to five percent, led by BellSouth Corp up 2-1/8 at 42-7/8 and the sixth most active stock on the New York Stock Exchange at 1445 EST/1945 GMT.
Long distance stocks were a little less strong, though AT&T Corp's 5/8 rise to 43-1/4 brought its gains since December 24 to almost 10 percent.
Klugman said that investors could be looking for value for 1997, given that the whole telecom sector drastically underperformed the broad market in 1996 so far.
The only recent news across the sector was a notice of Federal Communications Commission (FCC) rulemaking on access charges on December 24.

"It doesn't make sense that this is the reason," said Klugman, noting that this was just the start of a process on reforming access charges which could take a year including court challenges. -- Nick Louth, New York newsroom 212 859 1610
